pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #10
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is NOT a job of the roots? (1 mark)
   A. Holding the plant in the soil
   B. Making fruit
   C. Storing food in some plants
   D. Taking in water

2. Which of these is a good way to care for plants at school? (1 mark)
   A. Water them when the soil is dry
   B. Pick all the flowers
   C. Trample on flower beds
   D. Throw litter on them

3. Which part of a bean plant grows in the soil? (1 mark)
   A. Flowers
   B. Pods
   C. Roots
   D. Leaves

4. How do most flowering plants make new plants? (1 mark)
   A. By giving birth
   B. By seeds
   C. By laying eggs
   D. By walking away

5. In which part do you find the seeds of a mango? (1 mark)
   A. Leaf
   B. Stem
   C. Fruit
   D. Root

6. Which of these is a good way to care for a farm animal? (1 mark)
   A. Give it dirty water
   B. Give clean water and shelter
   C. Beat it
   D. Leave it in the rain

7. A goat lifts its head when it hears a noise. Which sign of life is this? (1 mark)
   A. Growing
   B. Breathing out
   C. Reproducing
   D. Responding to changes

8. Ostrich and flamingo belong to which group? (1 mark)
   A. Birds
   B. Mammals
   C. Amphibians
   D. Reptiles

9. Which of these animals is an amphibian? (1 mark)
   A. Snake
   B. Toad
   C. Tortoise
   D. Goat

10. Another name for the gullet is (1 mark)
   A. Oesophagus
   B. Tongue
   C. Rectum
   D. Anus

11. The stomach is described in the lesson as being like (1 mark)
   A. A hard stone
   B. A sharp knife
   C. A long ladder
   D. A stretchy bag

12. An empty bottle is full of (1 mark)
   A. Sand
   B. Nothing
   C. Air
   D. Water

13. What happens to a liquid when you pour it into a different container? (1 mark)
   A. It disappears
   B. It keeps its old shape
   C. It takes the shape of the new container
   D. It becomes a solid

14. Which of these is heavier: 3 kg of sugar or 3000 g of sugar? (1 mark)
   A. They have the same mass
   B. Cannot tell
   C. 3 kg
   D. 3000 g

15. A heavy sack of maize has more mass than a small packet of salt. This means the sack has more (1 mark)
   A. Sound
   B. Matter
   C. Air only
   D. Light

16. Which unit is used for the volume of milk? (1 mark)
   A. Metre
   B. Kilogram
   C. Litre
   D. Gram

17. What should you do after handling waste? (1 mark)
   A. Wash hands with soap and clean water
   B. Touch your face
   C. Wipe hands on your clothes
   D. Eat at once

18. Why is polythene dangerous for goats and cows? (1 mark)
   A. It makes them sweet
   B. They may eat it and get sick
   C. It makes them grow
   D. It makes milk

19. What does the word biodegradable mean? (1 mark)
   A. Able to be broken down by living things
   B. Made of glass
   C. Made of plastic
   D. Not able to rot

20. What should never be done with waste in a place where children are playing? (1 mark)
   A. Collect it
   B. Put it in a bin
   C. Burn it
   D. Sort it

21. Which of these reduces water use when brushing teeth? (1 mark)
   A. Leaving the tap running
   B. Using a hose
   C. Using a cup of water
   D. Using a bucket of water

22. What is rainwater harvesting? (1 mark)
   A. Selling rainwater
   B. Drinking rainwater from puddles
   C. Digging wells
   D. Catching and storing rainwater

23. What should be done with stored rainwater before drinking? (1 mark)
   A. Freeze it only
   B. Drink it directly
   C. Add soil
   D. Boil or treat it

24. Which of these helps farmers to save water? (1 mark)
   A. Leaving canals leaking
   B. Watering at noon
   C. Drip irrigation
   D. Flooding the field

25. Which of these is a way of wasting water? (1 mark)
   A. Closing taps
   B. Fixing leaks
   C. Leaving a tap running
   D. Using a bucket

26. Which surface gives the least friction? (1 mark)
   A. Rough sandpaper
   B. Dry grass
   C. A thick carpet
   D. A wet, oiled tile

27. What effect of force is shown when a goalkeeper stops a ball? (1 mark)
   A. Starts a moving object
   B. Stops a moving object
   C. Makes it lighter
   D. Changes its colour

28. What should you do when doing force experiments? (1 mark)
   A. Push others
   B. Keep fingers away from moving parts
   C. Run with sharp tools
   D. Throw heavy things

29. Which of these can change the shape of dough? (1 mark)
   A. Leaving it alone
   B. Pressing with a force
   C. Talking to it
   D. Looking at it

30. Which of these makes its own light? (1 mark)
   A. A shiny cup
   B. A white wall
   C. A glow-worm
   D. A mirror

31. What is the purpose of skylights? (1 mark)
   A. Block light
   B. Let daylight through the roof
   C. Let rain in on purpose
   D. Make the house hot

32. What does a translucent roof sheet do? (1 mark)
   A. Blocks all light
   B. Lets some light in
   C. Makes light
   D. Creates sound

33. What should you use to hold a hot cooking pot? (1 mark)
   A. Bare hands
   B. Kitchen gloves or a thick dry cloth
   C. Wet cloth
   D. A plastic bag

34. Which of these passes heat slowly? (1 mark)
   A. Copper
   B. Iron
   C. Wood
   D. Aluminium

35. Which is a correct statement about heat? (1 mark)
   A. It moves from a warm object to a cooler one
   B. It has mass
   C. It stays still
   D. It moves from cold to warm

36. Why is a thermometer better than touching to find how hot something is? (1 mark)
   A. It is noisy
   B. It is dangerous
   C. It is heavy
   D. It is safe and gives a number

37. In which unit is temperature measured in science? (1 mark)
   A. Kilograms
   B. Litres
   C. Metres
   D. Degrees Celsius

38. What should you never do with oil that is on fire? (1 mark)
   A. Move away
   B. Pour water on it
   C. Call for help
   D. Cover it with a lid

39. What should you do first if you burn your skin? (1 mark)
   A. Ignore it
   B. Put it under cool running water and tell an adult
   C. Put butter on it
   D. Cover it with soil

40. Which of these materials passes heat quickly? (1 mark)
   A. Metal
   B. Dry cloth
   C. Wood
   D. Plastic

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Explain the difference between diarrhoea and constipation. (4 marks)

42. Explain what would happen to a young bean plant if all its leaves were removed and why. (4 marks)

43. State three ways of keeping teeth healthy. (3 marks)

44. Why should we use LED and solar lamps instead of paraffin lamps? Give two reasons. (4 marks)

45. A jug holds 500 ml of water. Musa pours in 250 ml and later takes out 100 ml. How much water is in the jug at the end? (4 marks)

46. Explain what gravity is and give two examples of its effects. (3 marks)

47. Describe the function of each part of the digestive system: mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine and large intestine. (5 marks)

48. Explain why burning waste is not a good way of managing waste and give better methods. (5 marks)

49. A family of five uses a tap that drips 1 litre every hour. Calculate how much water is wasted in one week and suggest what they should do. (5 marks)

50. Draw and label a plant showing roots, stem, leaves and flower. (4 marks)

51. Describe the methods of conserving water. Include reducing, reusing and recycling with examples. (5 marks)

52. Explain how gravity helps and how it can cause problems in daily life. (5 marks)

53. Make a plan for keeping your digestive system healthy for one week. (5 marks)

54. List four signs of life in plants. (2 marks)

55. Give two examples of decomposable waste and two of non-decomposable waste. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #10 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Making fruit
   Fruits are made from flowers, not by roots.

2. A — Water them when the soil is dry
   Watering when dry helps plants live and grow.

3. C — Roots
   Roots grow underground.

4. B — By seeds
   Most flowering plants reproduce by making seeds inside fruits.

5. C — Fruit
   Seeds are found inside fruits.

6. B — Give clean water and shelter
   Farm animals need water, food, shelter and care.

7. D — Responding to changes
   The goat responds to a change in its surroundings, a sound.

8. A — Birds
   Both have feathers and lay eggs.

9. B — Toad
   Toads have moist skin and start life in water.

10. A — Oesophagus
   The gullet is also called the oesophagus.

11. D — A stretchy bag
   The stomach is a stretchy bag that churns food.

12. C — Air
   An empty bottle contains air.

13. C — It takes the shape of the new container
   A liquid has no shape of its own.

14. A — They have the same mass
   3 kg equals 3000 g.

15. B — Matter
   Mass is the amount of matter.

16. C — Litre
   Liquid volume is measured in millilitres and litres.

17. A — Wash hands with soap and clean water
   Washing removes germs.

18. B — They may eat it and get sick
   Animals that eat polythene can become ill or die.

19. A — Able to be broken down by living things
   Biodegradable waste rots naturally.

20. C — Burn it
   Burning near children is dangerous.

21. C — Using a cup of water
   A cup uses only a little water.

22. D — Catching and storing rainwater
   Harvesting means collecting rainwater from roofs.

23. D — Boil or treat it
   Boiling or treating kills germs.

24. C — Drip irrigation
   Drip irrigation gives water directly to roots.

25. C — Leaving a tap running
   A running tap that is not in use wastes water.

26. D — A wet, oiled tile
   Oil and smoothness reduce friction.

27. B — Stops a moving object
   The force of the hands stops the ball.

28. B — Keep fingers away from moving parts
   Safe practice prevents injuries.

29. B — Pressing with a force
   A force can squeeze and stretch dough.

30. C — A glow-worm
   Glow-worms produce their own light.

31. B — Let daylight through the roof
   Skylights are roof openings or sheets that let light in.

32. B — Lets some light in
   It lets daylight in but you cannot see through it clearly.

33. B — Kitchen gloves or a thick dry cloth
   Gloves stop heat reaching your hand.

34. C — Wood
   Wood is a poor passer of heat.

35. A — It moves from a warm object to a cooler one
   Heat moves from hot to cold.

36. D — It is safe and gives a number
   A thermometer avoids burns and measures.

37. D — Degrees Celsius
   Temperature is measured in degrees Celsius.

38. B — Pour water on it
   Water on burning oil spreads the fire.

39. B — Put it under cool running water and tell an adult
   Cool water reduces the burn.

40. A — Metal
   Metals pass heat easily.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Diarrhoea is passing loose watery faeces many times and causes loss of water. Constipation is passing hard dry faeces with difficulty.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each condition.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: The plant would become weak and stop growing. Leaves make food for the plant. Roots can take in water but without leaves the plant cannot make enough food.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for weak or stops growing, 1 mark for leaves make food, 1 mark for no food made, 1 mark for roots alone are not enough.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Brush at least twice a day, limit sweets and sugary drinks, visit a dentist, use clean toothbrush or chewing stick.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: They are safer with less fire risk and less smoke. Solar lamps use free energy and are cheaper to use.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each reason.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: 650 ml.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 500 + 250 = 750, 1 mark for 750 - 100, 1 mark for 650, 1 mark for the unit ml.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Gravity is the force that pulls objects towards the Earth. It makes rain fall and makes a thrown ball come down.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for each example.

47. (5 marks)
   Answer: Mouth: chews and adds saliva. Gullet: pushes food down. Stomach: churns with juices. Small intestine: finishes digestion and absorbs food. Large intestine: takes back water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

48. (5 marks)
   Answer: Burning gives harmful smoke, especially from plastic. Better: reduce, reuse, recycle, compost and use bins.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for reasons and 3 marks for better methods.

49. (5 marks)
   Answer: 24 x 7 = 168 litres. They should repair the tap or ask an adult or plumber to fix it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 24 hours, 1 mark for 24 x 7, 1 mark for 168, 1 mark for fixing the tap, 1 mark for units.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: A drawing with four correctly labelled parts: roots below the ground, stem upright, leaves on the stem and a flower at the top.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correctly drawn and labelled part.

51. (5 marks)
   Answer: Reduce wastage: close taps. Reuse: washing vegetables water on plants. Recycle: cleaning used water at a treatment plant or filtering. Include rainwater harvesting.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of three methods, 1 mark for correct examples and 1 mark for harvesting.

52. (5 marks)
   Answer: It keeps us on the ground, makes rain fall and water flow downhill. It can make objects fall and cause injuries and break things.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for help and 2 marks for problems and 1 mark for a clear explanation.

53. (5 marks)
   Answer: A plan including brushing teeth twice a day, eating fruits and vegetables, drinking clean water, washing hands, chewing well, deworming as advised and limiting sweets.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible action up to 5.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: Any four of: grow, reproduce, remove waste, respond to changes, die.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two correct signs and 2 marks for four correct signs.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: Decomposable: vegetable peelings, dung, leaves. Non-decomposable: plastic, tin, glass.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair.
